items.h: Ukrainian drones hit the Kirishi refinery as Russia strikes Odesa region's grid
items.body: The Kyiv Independent reported, citing monitoring channels and NASA fire data, that Ukrainian drones struck the Kirishi refinery, about 800 km from Ukraine and more than 6% of Russian refining, overnight into 9 Nov; Leningrad region's governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said “a total of 113 Ukrainian drones were shot down over the region” and that debris hit a flat without injuries. [15, 23] On the evening of 8 Nov Odesa's regional head Oleh Kiper said “Odesa region has come under a massive enemy attack on its energy infrastructure.” [24] The IAEA said the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost all off-site power for about 10 hours on 8 Nov; Rafael Grossi: “It is the 27th such event during the conflict.” [16] President Zelensky counted 115 missiles, nearly 1,900 guided bombs and more than 3,000 drones in the past week; Ukraine's General Staff put Russian losses in the day to 9 Nov at 2,980 personnel and 1,843 drones. [25, 26] At 04:21 Kyiv time the Air Force was still tracking jet-powered drones toward Kyiv, Zhytomyr and Mykolaiv regions, with no overnight total published. [27] NOS, citing Bloomberg, reported on 9 Nov that hacked civil death records show 392,700 deaths that reference the war from February 2022 to August 2026; Rosstat confirmed cyberattacks but denied that confidential data were taken. [28, 29]
items.next: US–Russia–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov; French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot: “France will be in Abu Dhabi to take part in these discussions.” [12]

items.h: Iran's Guards say three more tankers burned in Hormuz; Washington asks Iraq to shut crossings
items.body: The Revolutionary Guards said on 8 Nov that “three non-compliant tankers have exploded and caught fire while they were sailing in the illegal channel in the Strait of Hormuz”, without names or flags; AFP could not match them to the tanker fire UKMTO reported off Khasab on 7 Nov. [19] Fars said explosions heard at Bandar Abbas and Qeshm on the evening of 8 Nov may have been warning shots at ships. [30] Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said the US Treasury asked Iraq to close all but two of its border crossings with Iran: “Closing the border crossings could be a punishment for Iran, but it would also hurt Iraq.” [20] Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi wrote on X: “Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results.” [31] Secretary of State Rubio: “I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough.” [32] A drone hit Iraq's Khor Mor gas field on the night of 8 Nov and left more than 70% of the Kurdish region without power. [33]
items.next: President Trump hosts Qatar's prime minister at the White House on 9 Nov; G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris on 9–10 Nov. [34, 9]

items.h: Eisenkot gets the mandate as Gaza's storm kills five in a tent camp
items.body: President Herzog formally gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government on 8 Nov, with 28 days and a possible 14-day extension, after 67 Knesset members recommended him and 46 Netanyahu; Eisenkot pledged a “national emergency government”. [35] In Gaza a storm-driven collapse of sand onto tents in Deir al-Balah killed a woman and four children late on 8 Nov, and the health ministry's director-general said 350,000 displaced people were sleeping in the open. [36, 37] In Riyadh the energy ministry said “falling shrapnel” damaged an Aramco office building in the financial district on 8 Nov after an attempted Houthi attack, with no casualties; the coalition said it destroyed three ballistic-missile launchers, one in Sanaa and two in Saada. [38, 39]
items.next: The new Knesset is sworn in on 10 Nov. [40]

items.h: Moscow claims hits on three cargo ships off Odesa; Moldova logs two more balloon crossings
items.body: Russia's defence ministry said on 8 Nov it struck two container ships, one bound for Odesa and one in Chornomorsk, and a dry-cargo ship south-west of Odesa overnight; Reuters could not verify the claim and no Ukrainian source confirmed it. [41] Moldova's defence ministry said two aerostat-type objects crossed its airspace in Drochia and Soroca districts on the morning of 8 Nov, after 69 violations this year. [42, 43] President Maia Sandu: “In the coming months and beyond, we will see new attempts by the Russian Federation to destabilize the situation.” [44] Romania's defence ministry reported no airspace incursion during the 5–6 Nov attacks on Ukraine's Danube ports. [45]
items.next: Transnistria's unrecognised leadership vote is due in December, date not set. [46]

items.h: One PLA sortie near Taiwan in 24 hours; Washington protests Papua New Guinea's closure order
items.body: Taiwan's defence ministry said “1 sortie of PLA aircraft, 7 PLAN ships and 1 official ship operating around Taiwan were detected as of 6 a.m. (UTC+8) today”, 9 Nov, the sortie entering the northern air defence identification zone. [47] After Taiwan said it would close its office in Papua New Guinea, open since 1990, a State Department spokesman said: “This is yet another example of Beijing's intimidation campaign against Taiwan and its supporters around the world.” [48] KCNA reported on 9 Nov that Workers' Party secretary Kim Song-nam held talks with the head of the Chinese party's International Liaison Department and visited the Central Party School. [49, 50]
items.next: President Trump said he will discuss Iran with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at next week's APEC summit in China. [51]

feature.title: The Black Sea and Moldova in numbers: nine ships hit in October, 69 airspace violations in Moldova
body: In 24 days of October, aerial or naval drones hit nine merchant ships off Bulgaria and Romania, and AP counted at least 30 sailors dead or missing. [52] Reuters' list runs from the Royad Mammadov, hit 30 nautical miles south of Sfântu Gheorghe on 5 Oct with two dead, to the Contship Jet, which sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone on 28 Oct; the Alfa Watan sank with 12 missing, the HS Dignity off Krapets with 11 missing, and the Khoryv off Constanța. [53]

Romania's defence ministry gave ABC News a count in May of 25 Russian drone violations of its airspace since 2022, nine of them in 2025 and seven in 2026 to 28 April, and 47 finds of munition fragments, 11 of them in 2026. [54] Ukraine's Sea Ports Authority said its ports handled “more than 27 million tonnes of cargo” from January to late April 2026, and that “172 civilian vessels have been damaged or partially destroyed” since the full-scale invasion. [55]

The allied answer at sea is small. The mine-countermeasures group of Romania, Bulgaria and Türkiye, operational since 1 July 2024, had completed 10 activations by July 2026, when its mandate was widened to the protection of critical undersea infrastructure, with Bulgaria in command from 9 July. [56] On the far side of the Prut, Moldova's defence ministry counts 69 airspace violations in 2026 and 106 since 2022. [43]

leads.title: A pro-Russian group posts a bounty list of 18 Europeans, from Italy's foreign minister to a Frankfurt prosecutor
leads.teaser: The Tajani doxxing turns out to be one page of a wider list that names the people who investigate the group, and offers money for more.
rows: Il Sole 24 Ore reported on 7 Nov that NoName057(16) posted a Tor-only “Tribunale” page listing 18 “enemies of the Russian Federation”, with emails, phone numbers and social-media profiles, and offers payment for more information. [21]

Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, Rome's chief prosecutor Francesco Lo Voi, postal-police chief Ivano Gabrielli, Eurojust's Michael Schmid, Europol cybercrime centre head Edvardas Šileris, Frankfurt prosecutor Benjamin Krause, three German investigative journalists and the mayor of Aviano, home of the US Air Force base. [21, 58]

A2. Claimed by the group; Rome prosecutors opened an investigation and Il Sole calls a Russian directive a hypothesis, which Moscow denies. Tajani: “Siamo di fronte ad una guerra ibrida”, we are facing a hybrid war. [21]
Tajani said he asked the G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris on 9–10 Nov to take it up; he told La Voce he “non mi farò intimidire in nessun modo”, will not be intimidated in any way. [21, 58]
leads.sw: A list that pays for personal data on prosecutors, police and a base-town mayor is a force-protection question for allied staff and families across the Joint Operations Area, not only a cyber case; check what the Brunssum security office advises on personal data online.

leads.title: No new airliner hoax over the weekend; Dublin readies 55 leaders under a “substantial” threat rating
leads.teaser: The wave of 2–6 Nov has paused, and the next big target set, the European Political Community summit on Thursday, has Dutch and French drone police on standby.
rows: Air Journal on 8 Nov listed Friday's four alerts, three landings at Orly and one at Bordeaux, as the latest; no new threat or arrest was reported on 7–8 Nov. [59]

A1. The Irish Examiner reported on 7 Nov that security services assess as credible that Russian intelligence was behind the coordinated threats, while sources say it is very hard to prove; the Russian embassy in Dublin called the link “totally unfounded”. [60] Hungary's defence minister wrote on 8 Nov that the frequency and spread point to possible coordination. [61]

The Garda rates the likelihood of cyberattack, drone incursion, bomb threats or disruptive protest as “substantial”, third of five levels; specialist drone police teams from France and the Netherlands support gardaí. Taoiseach Micheál Martin: “it's the largest ever security operation in the history of the State”. [60, 62]
European Political Community summit on Thu 12 Nov and informal EU leaders' meeting on Fri 13 Nov. [62]
leads.sw: Dutch police drone teams in Dublin are capacity the Netherlands is not using at home that week; baseline requirement 7 (civil transportation) is the line to watch if the hoaxes return around the summit.

pattern: **From leaks to bounties:** NoName057(16) now pays for data on the prosecutors, police and journalists who investigate it, and names a US base town's mayor. [21]

**Operators get drone powers:** Czechia's cabinet reviews today a draft letting airports, energy hubs and nuclear plants bring down drones in protected zones, as the Netherlands studies the same. [63]
**Rail again, near us:** signal-box damage and vandalism near Cologne are under state-security investigation. [57]
**Recruitment through study:** Estonia's security police warn that about 400 Estonian students in Russia face recruitment. [64]

europe.h: Poland opens a terrorism case over Kraków as the toll reaches nine with the gunman's family
europe.body: The National Prosecutor's Office opened an investigation on 8 Nov into the killing of six people on the Rynek Główny as a terrorist offence, and into the deaths of the suspect's parents and sister in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski; the 24-year-old suspect is in critical condition and not yet formally detained. [65] Prime Minister Donald Tusk: “Senior Constable Jakub Kulik and Senior Constable Artur Moranski are true heroes.” Two days of national mourning were declared and the St Mary's trumpet call fell silent for 12 hours, the first such pause since 1939. [66, 67]
europe.sw: Independence Day marches follow on 11 Nov; Warsaw police have already reinforced tourist areas, a baseline requirement 5 (mass casualties) posture in a frontline ally.

europe.h: France will sit at the Abu Dhabi table as G7 ministers meet Rubio in Paris
europe.body: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot told RTL on 8 Nov: “Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks”; G7 foreign ministers meet at the Quai d'Orsay on 9–10 Nov with Secretary Rubio. [68, 9] Jared Kushner says Washington is working on “a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace”; Kaja Kallas: “We already have a European security architecture in place.” [68, 69]
europe.sw: European presence in Abu Dhabi decides whether the posture and force-sharing assumptions in JFC Brunssum's regional plans are negotiated with allies in the room.

europe.h: De Wever restarts Belgian budget talks one-on-one as a minister and the US envoy trade insults
europe.body: VRT reported on 8 Nov that the Prime Minister is opting for “bilaterale gesprekken met de vicepremiers afzonderlijk”, separate talks with each deputy prime minister, from Monday, with more on Tuesday; he reports to the Palace on 16 Nov. [70] Flemish minister Zuhal Demir and US Ambassador Bill White exchanged posts on X over her calling President Trump “het Oranje gevaar”. [70]
europe.sw: NATO's and SHAPE's host stays on provisional twelfths until at least 16 Nov, holding Belgian defence commitments at this year's level.

countries.h: Hungary's defence minister calls the airliner bomb threats a possible coordinated campaign
countries.body: Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi wrote on 8 Nov, relayed by the defence forces' site, that the frequency, spread and timing of the threats point to possible coordinated action aimed at disrupting European air traffic and testing allied responses; on one day Hungary had three alerts in a row, each met by a Gripen scramble. [61] He wrote that Gripens identify and track a threatened airliner and could act “with kinetic means” only with legal authority, which a bomb threat alone does not give, and that Hungary keeps round-the-clock readiness inside NATO's integrated air and missile defence. [61]
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 7 (civil transportation): the hoax wave has reached quick-reaction alert in Central Europe, and Budapest now frames it as a NATO air-defence matter.

q.t: A honvédelmi miniszter szerint ezek a fenyegetések jóval túlmutatnak az egyes légijáratokat érintő biztonsági incidenseken.
q.en: According to the defence minister, these threats go far beyond security incidents affecting individual flights.

countries.h: Poland and Czechia join Hungary's regional energy coalition as the Adria spill clean-up runs ten days
countries.body: Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány said on 8 Nov that Poland and Czechia joined an expanded Central and Southern European energy coalition with Italy at a meeting in Zagreb on Black Sea gas, supply routes and market integration: “folytatni fogjuk két hét múlva Bukarestben”, we will continue in Bucharest in two weeks. [71] Croatia's JANAF said about 500 m³ of crude spilled from the Adria line near Prvča, with clean-up expected to take ten days; whether deliveries to Hungary were interrupted has not been disclosed. [72]
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 2 (energy): Hungary's crude rests on Druzhba and Adria, and Adria is Hungary's alternative to Druzhba; a ten-day repair with no restart date is the gap to watch.

q.t: Egyelőre nem közölték, hogy a sérült vezetékszakasz leállítása okozott-e fennakadást a Magyarországra irányuló szállításokban.
q.en: It has not yet been disclosed whether shutting the damaged section disrupted deliveries to Hungary.

countries.h: Fico hands back the environment ministry as Taraba's three MPs refuse a key coalition bill
countries.body: Prime Minister Robert Fico returns the mandate to run the environment ministry to President Peter Pellegrini today and proposes a Slovak National Party nominee, ending his own caretaker role amid the dispute between SNS leader Andrej Danko and former minister Tomáš Taraba. [73] Taraba told Joj 24 on 8 Nov that he and his two MPs will not back the cooperating-witness amendment to the criminal procedure code; Szalay of the opposition SaS: “Vtedy sa ukáže, či majú 76 (poslancov)”, then we will see whether they have 76 MPs. [74, 75] Parliament resumes on Tue 10 Nov with a voting block and a pending constitutional amendment allowing a referendum to end the term. [76]
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 1 (continuity of government): a coalition below 76 votes passes bills case by case, which slows any defence or civil-preparedness law through 2027.

q.t: Premiér Robert Fico (Smer-SD) vráti v pondelok (9. 11.) prezidentovi SR Petrovi Pellegrinimu poverenie na riadenie Ministerstva životného prostredia (MŽP) SR.
q.en: Prime Minister Robert Fico (Smer-SD) will on Monday (9 Nov) return to President Peter Pellegrini the mandate to run the Ministry of Environment.

countries.h: Pellegrini takes Ukraine and energy security to Macron on Wednesday
countries.body: President Peter Pellegrini attends the Paris Peace Forum on Tue 10 Nov, dines at the Élysée and meets President Macron on 11 Nov on the strategic partnership, “rozširovanie EÚ, Ukrajina, európska energetická bezpečnosť a regionálna spolupráca” during Slovakia's Visegrád presidency, EU enlargement, Ukraine, European energy security and regional cooperation. [77]
countries.sw: A president who backs Ukraine's EU path abroad while the government doubts it at home is the split the profile tracks under stance.

q.t: Prezident SR Peter Pellegrini odcestuje v utorok (10. 11.) na deviaty ročník Parížskeho mierového fóra.
q.en: President Peter Pellegrini will travel on Tuesday (10 Nov) to the ninth Paris Peace Forum.

countries.h: German gas storage stands at 60.2%, well below past years, the network agency says
countries.body: The Bundesnetzagentur's assessment of 6 Nov, updated 8 Nov, puts storage at 60.2% or 149 TWh and adds that “Ein vergleichsweise niedriger Speicherfüllstand am Ende des Winters ist wahrscheinlich”, a comparatively low level at the end of winter is probable, while it rates the risk of a tight supply as low; the early-warning stage of the gas emergency plan has applied since 1 Jul 2025. [78]
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 2 (energy): low German storage going into winter is the host-nation energy margin behind reinforcement through North Rhine-Westphalia and Lower Saxony.

q.t: Die Füllstände der Speicher in Deutschland liegen derzeit bei 60,2 % (149 TWh).
q.en: Storage levels in Germany currently stand at 60.2% (149 TWh).

countries.h: The Bundestag closes the 2027 budget this week, with about €140 billion for defence
countries.body: The budget committee meets on Wed 11 Nov and holds its final clean-up session on Thu 12 Nov, running into Friday morning, with the plenary vote planned for 23–27 Nov. [79] The defence ministry's draft gives about €110 billion in its own budget and about €30 billion from the special fund, rising to about €152 billion by 2029, when Germany intends to reach NATO's 3.5% core target “sechs Jahre früher als vom Bündnis gefordert”, six years earlier than the Alliance requires. [80]
countries.sw: The clean-up session is where defence lines get trimmed or protected; the 2027 number sets German host-nation and reinforcement capacity for the regional plans.

q.t: Bis voraussichtlich in die frühen Morgenstunden des Freitags wird der Haushalt bereinigt.
q.en: The budget will be finalised, probably into the early hours of Friday.

countries.h: The Kremlin says Moscow has had no contact with Europeans on a security agreement
countries.body: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told state television on 8 Nov, in TASS's English rendering of the state's own words: “As far as we know, the Americans have indeed had contacts with the Europeans. We have had no contacts with the Europeans.” [17]
countries.sw: The state's own words put Europe outside any Russia–US track on European security, the day before Abu Dhabi.

countries.h: Lukashenko sends condolences to Poland over Kraków as Lithuania turns back seven migrants
countries.body: BelTA published Lukashenko's message of 8 Nov, the state's own words: “искренние соболезнования всему польскому народу”, sincere condolences to the entire Polish people. [81] Lithuania's border guard said it turned back seven irregular migrants at the Belarusian border in 24 hours. [82]
countries.sw: A conciliatory message to Warsaw sits beside continued pressure at the Lithuanian line; the profile logs both.

countries.h: China's rare-earth control pause runs out on 10 Nov with no extension posted
countries.body: As of about 12:30 Beijing time on 9 Nov, neither the commerce ministry's homepage nor its export-control bureau listed a notice extending Announcement No. 70, which suspends the October 2025 rare-earth and battery-materials controls until 10 Nov. [83] On 6 Nov the ministry opened an anti-dumping case into para-aramid filament from the EU, whose listed uses include ballistic fabrics. [84]
countries.sw: German magnet and munitions supply chains depend on the pause; ask the German liaison whether firms have stockpiled for a lapse.

euregio.h: Schiphol bids for 80% of Maastricht Aachen Airport; L1 puts the province's extra bill at €130 million
euregio.body: The airport said on 5 Nov that Royal Schiphol Group wants to raise its stake from 40% to 80%, subject to “verdere besluitvorming en definitieve afspraken”, further decisions and final agreements, with the province keeping 20% if Provinciale Staten agree. [85] L1 reported on 8 Nov that the province, which has put in more than €100 million since 2022, would carry an estimated further €130 million against Schiphol's pledged €33 million. [86]
euregio.fy: Nothing changes for flights from Maastricht this winter; the Staten vote has no date yet.

euregio.h: Flanders' leader urges support for Ukraine at the German war cemetery in Lommel
euregio.body: At the Volkstrauertag ceremony on 8 Nov at the cemetery of 39,000 German dead, Minister-President Matthias Diependaele said: “Poetin is een dictator en hij gaat nooit concessies doen of een compromis sluiten”, Putin is a dictator who will never compromise, and “daarom vind ik dat we Oekraïne moeten steunen om die Russische pletwals tegen te houden”. [87] Lommel is about 60 km from Heerlen.
euregio.fy: The cemetery is open year round and is a sober half-day with a teenager interested in history.

items.h: Koalicja 26.2 opens in Poland with 2,800 allied troops and no US units
items.body: The first exercise of the Multinational Force–Ukraine runs from today to 22 Nov with troops from 11 nations; France brings a unit with about 50 contact drones, Poland adds nearly 2,000 soldiers beyond the foreign contingents, and Türkiye leads the maritime element from Istanbul without sending troops to Poland. [88] UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting: “This exercise shows the UK is stepping up.” [88] It is not under NATO command. [89]
items.sw: Dutch, Belgian and German units train for a mission outside NATO command; their availability to JFC Brunssum's regional plans while earmarked for Ukraine is the force-generation question.

items.h: More than 6,000 troops exercise in Lithuania under Germany's 45th Panzer Brigade
items.body: Freedom Shield 26-II and Grand Eagle 26 run from 6 Nov to 3 Dec at the Rūdninkai and Gen. Silvestras Žukauskas training areas with the German brigade based in Lithuania, the 37th Mechanised Infantry Brigade of the 10th Armoured Division and the Multinational Brigade Lithuania contingents, Dutch and Belgian among them; convoys move from Klaipėda on 10–12 Nov. [90, 91]
items.sw: A permanently based German brigade exercising with its reinforcing division is the model JFC Brunssum's regional plans assume for the Baltic.

items.h: Romania offers to pay toward a permanent US presence and revives the SkyCeptor interceptor
items.body: DefenseRomania reported on 6 Nov that Romania's defence ministry has sent Washington an offer for a permanent US presence with cost-sharing “on the Polish model”, citing “very encouraging signals”; the ministry, unnamed, said deploying elements of a unit such as the 101st Airborne Division “would send an extremely strong deterrence message”. [92] It is also reopening talks with Rafael to build the SkyCeptor interceptor for Patriot at Electromecanica Ploiești, at about $1 million a round against $4–5 million for a Patriot missile. [93]

research.org: Center for a New American Security (CNAS)
research.title: Munitions Procurement and the Fiscal Year 2027 Defense Budget: Three Conditions for Munitions Acceleration
summary: Haelig starts from the war with Iran, which has drawn down US munitions faster than they can be replaced, and reads the Department of War's FY27 request as the answer: “Across the 10 offensive strike weapons and defensive interceptors analyzed in this report, the DoW requested $49.5 billion in procurement funding, which is over eight times the average annual procurement funding enacted for these munitions from FY16–26 (in constant FY27 dollars).” The surge is front-loaded and mostly carried by reconciliation, and planned spending falls back to a plateau after FY27. His verdict: the budget “is a necessary but insufficient vehicle for closing munitions shortfalls.” [121]

Three conditions must hold at once: multi-year money, faster conversion of budgets into contracts, and an industrial base that delivers at scale. Of these, “the hardest of the three to move—and the one that ultimately governs how quickly the magazine refills—is production capacity.” The justification books show no gain in speed so far: “Of the seven programs covered in this report with FY27 contract plans in place, none are slated to deliver munitions requested in the FY27 budget any faster than those munitions ordered prior to the munitions acceleration push.” He recommends on-time appropriations, an executable reconciliation bill, turning the seven-year framework agreements into multiyear contracts, moving the surge into the base budget and buying cheaper munitions that can be built faster. [121]
findings: **Scale:** $49.5 billion requested for the 10 munitions in FY27 against an FY16–26 average of $5.8 billion a year in FY27 dollars, “an 8.5 times increase”. [121]

**Money source:** 82% of the FY27 request ($40.5 billion) comes through reconciliation, against 36% ($3.4 billion) in FY26; the plan then averages $26.7 billion a year through FY31, “a 46 percent decline” from FY27. [121]
**Stocks used:** estimates put 53–81% of THAAD and 45–61% of PAC-3 inventories expended by April 2026, with at least 32% of Tomahawks and 25% of available JASSMs used. [121]

**Capacity:** the FY27 books still cap THAAD at 96 a year against an FY27 order of 857; whether PAC-3 MSE can rise from 550 to 2,000 a year is uncertain, and lead times are unchanged for 6 of the 10 munitions. [121]
**Slower, not faster:** award-to-delivery times on FY27 contracts lengthen by 2 months for PAC-3 MSE, 4 months for SM-6 and Tomahawk and almost a year for the Air Force's AMRAAM. [121]
research.method: A reading of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force and Missile Defense Agency budget justification books for FY2018–FY2027, accessed 28 Aug 2026, in constant FY27 dollars, for 10 of the Munitions Acceleration Council's 14 priority munitions, with award-to-first-delivery times compared against each programme's pre-ramp baseline; inventory figures are other analysts' estimates. The author warns that out-year figures “represent plans rather than commitments”, that Congress may not appropriate the request, that emerging programmes such as the Joint Advanced Tactical Missile are excluded, and that the AMRAAM maximum rate “remains classified”. [121]
research.sw: For Brunssum: PAC-3, AMRAAM and SM-6 are the interceptors European allies are also queuing for, so a US magazine refilled by 2028 at the earliest is the planning assumption for air-defence stocks behind the Joint Force Command's regional plans; ask which allied orders sit behind US replenishment on the same production lines.

research.title: Rising Military Spending in the Context of Falling Development Assistance
summary: SIPRI compares military spending and official development assistance (ODA) across the 34 donor states of the OECD's Development Assistance Committee, with Germany and the UK as cases. Governments present aid cuts as paying for rearmament; the authors find that “financial savings from ODA reductions are small compared with the scale of planned increases in military spending”, and in Germany “the increase in military spending will be more than 10 times larger than the planned ODA reduction”. A model that ties aid to global need shows commitments “falling far below levels that would have been expected based on historical relationships between donor commitments and global needs.” Their conclusion: “There is a structural and worrying withdrawal of development assistance by DAC donors.” [122]
findings: DAC aid fell to $174 billion in 2025, 23% below 2024 and 0.26% of gross national income; “The decline in 2025 was the largest annual contraction in ODA ever recorded”. [122]

Germany: aid falls from 0.56% of GNI in 2025 to about 0.43% by 2029 while military spending rises from 2.3% to 3.5% of GDP and roughly doubles from $114 billion by 2030; 2025 procurement of about $96 billion was more than 3.5 times total aid. [122]
UK: aid is cut from 0.5% to 0.3% of GNI by 2027, freeing about $7.5 billion; the 2025–26 cut of $0.6 billion compares with a $5.6 billion military increase in 2026. [122]
Needs gap: $115 billion in 2028 alone under the baseline, $313 billion over 2026–28 (range $84–474 billion across scenarios). [122]
Conflict: 65 state-based conflicts in 2025, the most recorded by the Uppsala Conflict Data Program. [122]
research.method: OECD DAC data to October 2026 and the SIPRI Military Expenditure Database (April 2026), with an aid-needs index of 10 equally weighted variables (armed conflicts, battle deaths, violent events, disasters, displacement, a risk index and human development) regressed against commitments for 2005–21 by ordinary least squares (adjusted R² 0.79) and projected under three scenarios. The authors note the estimates “reflect historical donor responses to needs, rather than the level of financing required”, that equal weighting is built in, and that “A small sample size in empirical analysis affects the statistical power of estimates”. [122]
research.sw: The Sahel, Sudan and the Horn sit on the board as theatres; aid that falls while defence rises changes what Europe's neighbourhood looks like by 2028.

research.org: Demographic Research (Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research)
research.title: The impact of increased child benefits on tempo and quantum of fertility in Estonia
research.authors: Tanel Paas, Allan Puur and Mark Gortfelder
summary: “On July 1, 2017, Estonia introduced a substantial child allowance for families with three or more children, supplementing regular child benefits”: €500 a month for a three-child family, 41% of the average gross salary. The authors ask whether this universal, untested payment changed whether and when women had a third child. Their answer, from register data: “We find evidence that the reform was associated with a shortening of the time to third birth by nearly a quarter and a 4 percentage point increase in the probability of a third birth, corresponding to an 11% rise relative to the baseline third birth probability (37%).” The gain was uneven: “the positive quantum effect of the reform was concentrated among women with lower or medium income and education.” [123]
findings: Third-birth probability rose 4 points on a 37% baseline; second-birth probability fell 1.8 points. [123]
The wait from second birth to third conception shortened by 22% (time ratio 0.78). [123]
By income: odds of a third birth up 18% and 22% in the two lower quartiles, down 2% and 13% in the two upper ones; by education, up 23% for low and medium, down 14% for tertiary. [123]
Relative poverty among families with three or more children fell from 28.2% in 2016 to 16.5% in 2018; large-family benefits cost 0.39–0.43% of GDP in 2018–23. [123]
research.method: Longitudinal register data from Statistics Estonia for women born 1967–2006, observed 2005–24 (105,252 at risk of a second birth, 91,047 of a third), in a mixture-cure model inside a difference-in-differences design that uses women at risk of a second birth as the control. The authors note the design “relies on the assumption that, in the absence of the reform, both groups would have experienced similar trends”, that they “did not assess potential unintended consequences, such as changes in women's labour market participation”, and that the post-reform period is short. [123]
research.sw: Several NATO hosts, the Baltic states among them, now pay for births as a long-term manpower question; this is a measured effect, not a hope.

philosophy.where: First Section, Sixth Preliminary Article (Akademie edition VIII, 346–347)
philosophy.quote: “No state at war with another shall countenance such modes of hostility as would make mutual confidence impossible in a subsequent state of peace: such are the employment of assassins (percussores) or of poisoners (venefici), breaches of capitulation, the instigating and making use of treachery (perduellio) in the hostile state.” These are dishonourable stratagems. For some kind of confidence in the disposition of the enemy must exist even in the midst of war, as otherwise peace could not be concluded, and the hostilities would pass into a war of extermination (bellum internecinum).
philosophy.translation: M. Campbell Smith, London, 1903 (Project Gutenberg); the German: “Es soll sich kein Staat im Kriege mit einem andern solche Feindseligkeiten erlauben, welche das wechselseitige Zutrauen im künftigen Frieden unmöglich machen müssen”. [124]
philosophy.gloss: Kant's argument is not that such methods are cruel but that they destroy the one thing a war must leave standing if it is ever to end: a minimum of trust in the enemy's way of thinking. A war that consumes that trust tends toward extermination, which would bring perpetual peace “only in the great graveyard of the human race”, so the means that lead there are “absolutely forbidden”; and he adds that “these infernal arts, already vile in themselves, on coming into use, are not long confined to the sphere of war.” [125] The article is one of three he calls strict laws, binding whatever the circumstances, and it sits among negative duties that, in Frederick Rauscher's summary, prohibit acts “that would breed mistrust and make peace impossible”. [125, 126] The strongest objection is the just-war case made in Alexander Moseley's encyclopedia entry: killing one legitimate target “to avoid further bloodshed or to secure a quicker victory” seems to pass the tests of discrimination and proportionality, so a blanket ban looks unjustified. [127] Kant's reply is the second half of the passage, that the practice does not stay in war; Hobbes, whom he is answering, had written that “Force, and Fraud, are in warre the two Cardinall vertues.” [128]
philosophy.why: Which of the hybrid methods on today's board, hoax threats, sabotage of fridges, doxxing of ministers' families, would Kant have counted among the stratagems that make a later peace impossible, and does the answer change how we describe them?

deep.title: Hormuz, 1987–88: escorted tankers, a minelayer caught at night and a frigate's broken keel
body: In March 1987 the United States agreed to protect 11 Kuwaiti tankers in the Gulf, the start of Operation Earnest Will; in May two Iraqi missiles hit USS Stark and killed 37 sailors. [130] On 24 July the reflagged tanker Bridgeton struck a mine on the first escorted convoy. [130] On 21 September US forces caught the Iranian ship Iran Ajr laying mines. [130]

On 14 April 1988 the frigate Samuel B. Roberts struck an Iranian mine in the central Gulf, and its crew fought fire and flooding into the night; one of them, writing in 2021, dated the blast to 4:39 p.m. [130, 131] Four days later Operation Praying Mantis sank or heavily damaged five Iranian warships and smaller vessels. [130]

The echo is the sequence: an escort regime, mines laid at night by a state that denied laying them, and a reprisal that came only once a warship was hit. The difference today is that no ship has been named in three days of Iranian claims, and the escort regime is a US blockade of Iran rather than a convoy for Kuwait. [19]

otd.title: On this day · 9 November 1989
otd.body: At a live press conference in East Berlin, Politburo spokesman Günter Schabowski read out at 18:57 a draft rule that “Privatreisen nach dem Ausland können ohne Vorliegen von Voraussetzungen” be applied for, with permits “kurzfristig erteilt”, private travel abroad without preconditions, permits granted at short notice. [165] Asked when it took effect, he answered that to his knowledge it applied “sofort, unverzüglich”, immediately, without delay, though the rule was meant to start later and only on application. [165] Crowds gathered at the crossings, and at 23:14 the barriers opened at Bornholmer Straße; the guards at first stamped East German identity cards as void and later gave up checks altogether. [165]

culture.title: Weckmann: the Rhineland's St Martin bread, two days out
culture.body: Across the border, children who walk the St Martin lantern processions on Wednesday get a Weckmann afterwards, a figure of sweet yeast dough with raisin eyes: “Im Rheinland ist es Tradition, dass Kinder nach dem Martinsumzug einen Weckmann geschenkt bekommen”, in the Rhineland it is tradition that children receive a Weckmann after the procession. [166] The clay pipe on its chest began as something else: “Bei der Tonpfeife handelte es sich ursprünglich nicht um eine Pfeife, sondern einen Bischofsstab”, the pipe was originally a bishop's staff, from the figure's start as St Nicholas. [167] The Rhineland alone has more than 50 names for it, Stutenkerl in Westphalia among them. [166] On the Dutch side, Sint Maarten lantern walks run the same evening.

Discrepancies: CENTCOM's 147 vessels redirected (its 7 Nov statement) against 144 to the end of October (AP, Lloyd's List); 30 dead or missing in the Black Sea (AP) against 34 (an AFP-based count via Universul); the Khoryv's crew (Reuters: all rescued; Al Jazeera: three missing); Kraków injured 15, 16 or 17; Koalicja nations 10 (Euronews, Deutschlandfunk) or 11 counting Türkiye; the Saudi coalition spokesman's rank differs by outlet, so it is not given. Left out pending a second source or a readable page: Mélenchon's call to leave NATO and Barrot's rebuke (tagesschau and Le Monde headlines only); a cyberattack Moldova says touched 450,000 citizens (Moldpres headline only); Dodik's conditions for joining the state government (Sarajevo Times only); Merz on meeting Putin at the G20 (TASS rendering of a paywalled interview); the Hänneschen Christmas play and a Mayersche book evening (end dates or organiser pages not confirmed). Countries: every Hungary, Slovakia and Germany item quotes a .hu, .sk or .de source in the country's language; Russian, Belarusian and Chinese words are the states' own, via TASS, BelTA and MOFCOM. Profiles: confirmed on official pages Ryzhenkov (mfa.gov.by, 6 Nov), Lavrov and Belousov (government.ru) and Wang Yi (fmprc.gov.cn, 4 Nov); Dong Jun only as of the latest mod.gov.cn item, June 2026; Khrenin, the Medininkai and Šalčininkai crossings and any Belarusian units in Ukraine are not confirmed (mil.by and the Lithuanian border-guard sites were unreachable), so no context profile is marked verified.
